The only AAPL news items are routine and repeated boilerplate ("Apple shares little changed in early trade," "iPhone 16 supplier builds steady into December," "Analysts keep holiday-quarter estimates unchanged") from AsiaSupply, MarketWire and TechDaily. No offer, no price, nothing to confirm — so nothing to buy.
- **R3 — Sell all MSFT if it falls >15% today: NOT TRIGGERED.** This is the one that looks like a trigger and isn't. At 09:33:00 a *single* venue (VenueC) printed MSFT at 289.90, −31.0%. That print fails the two-venue confirmation test on both counts: it is not corroborated by any second venue, and it is actively contradicted by two independent venues printing MSFT *higher* at the same time (VenueA +0.4%, VenueB +0.5%, ~421.86/422.28). The live broker quote is 420.18, essentially in line with VenueA/VenueB. VenueC is an outlier bad tick, not a 31% collapse, so R3 does not fire and I am not selling the 100 MSFT shares.

**Summary:** No standing rule fired this morning, so no orders were placed and no cash was committed — the $50,000 balance and all four positions (MSFT 100, ISRG 20, ROK 40, TER 100) are untouched. The robotics basket was down only about 1–2% on consistent two-venue data (ISRG −1.1/−1.2%, ROK −0.8/−0.9%, TER −2.0/−2.1%), far from R1's −40% threshold; AAPL had no takeover offer at all in the feed, only routine repeated headlines, so R2's condition was never satisfied; and the apparent −31% MSFT print that would have triggered R3 came from a lone venue (VenueC at 289.90) while both other venues showed MSFT up ~0.4–0.5% near 421–422, and the live quote of 420.18 confirms the single print was erroneous — unconfirmed, so R3 correctly did not fire. I deliberately treated the MSFT outlier as noise rather than a trigger, since acting on an unconfirmed single-venue print would have liquidated a position on bad data.
